resolved_conflicts.explanation: HABS says continuous light since 1812; the USLHS roster starts 1811; the York museum says tower complete by winter 1811; NRHP says established during the War of 1812. The 1799 date in some lists is the wooden day beacon, not a light.
Current granite tower built 1854, first lit 1 Jan 1855 (HABS); earlier towers 1811 and 1831. Sources differ on whether 1831 was a new tower or a heightening.

notes_for_editor: Several facts rest on Lighthousefriends (secondary; its quotations of 1843/1888 reports, keeper logs and letters are second-hand and cited as such). Tower height is given as 118/123/133 ft by different sources and is stated as disagreeing in the text. The 1914 Bulletin rescue date (5 December) has no year: the Bulletin volume is 1914 and Radley's roster stint is 1913-14. The Gold Hunter crew count (six) is Lighthousefriends only; the Portland paper gives no count. Corpus reports for 1855-1890 are not in the local corpus, so the 1887 storm and 1888 report are from NRHP/HABS/Lighthousefriends. The 'tallest in Maine' claim follows the NRHP only. Roster lines not checked against NARA registers; USCG lines are the archive's own heading. The 1978 storm date in the York page is 'early February'. Fact-check 2026-10-27: Increase date disagrees (HABS April 1682, York museum summer 1682), now stated. Bulletin rescue year (1913 or 1914) remains open; 1901 report printed page not verified, cited by scan pages only.
